categories.title: Hubs and marketplaces
categories.blurb: Cross-platform places to browse and download. Start here if you do not know what you want yet.

categories.title: Platform scenes
categories.blurb: One console or computer per community. These are the databases, wikis and forums where each scene keeps its releases.

categories.title: Fantasy consoles and open handhelds
categories.blurb: Machines that exist to be programmed. Carts are tiny, shareable and playable in a browser tab.

categories.title: Hall of fame
categories.blurb: Homebrew games worth starting with, each made for real or fantasy hardware.

categories.title: Studios and cartridge makers
categories.blurb: Teams that release new games on physical cartridges for old consoles.

categories.title: Jams and competitions
categories.blurb: Deadlines produce games. These events produce a lot of them.

categories.title: Build your own
categories.blurb: Toolchains, engines and references for writing a game for hardware that shipped decades ago.

categories.title: Run it anywhere
categories.blurb: Emulators, FPGA, flash carts and handheld firmware for playing homebrew on a screen you like.

entries.name: Ported2Browser
entries.blurb: An independent directory of games ported to run in a browser tab, from Windows and DOS to arcade, consoles and handhelds. Filter by platform or tag, check whether a port supports keyboard, gamepad or touchscreen, and play on the creator's site.

entries.name: itch.io
entries.blurb: Indie marketplace with tag pages for Game Boy, NES, PICO-8 and most other retro targets. Many games are free or pay what you want.

entries.name: itch.io Game Boy tag
entries.blurb: Every itch.io game tagged Game Boy, from ROMs for real cartridges to GB Studio projects.

entries.name: itch.io NES tag
entries.blurb: NES games on itch.io. Some are 8-bit styled PC games, so read the platform line before downloading.

entries.name: itch.io PICO-8 tag
entries.blurb: PICO-8 games that run in the browser tab and export from the console as a single cart.

entries.name: itch.io homebrew tag
entries.blurb: Games that authors themselves labeled homebrew, across every platform on the site.

entries.name: Game Jolt
entries.blurb: Free indie and fan game platform with a Retro & Homebrew community where showcases, dev posts and console-specific jams are posted.

entries.name: GBAtemp
entries.blurb: Console hacking forum with release threads for GBA, DS, 3DS, Wii and Switch homebrew.

entries.name: ROMhacking.net
entries.blurb: Archive of ROM hacks, translations and utilities, with a separate section for original homebrew.

entries.name: Homebrew Factory
entries.blurb: Storefront for physical homebrew releases and crowdfunded preorders. Browse new games for old consoles and back the creators making cartridges.

entries.name: Homebrew Hub
entries.blurb: Game Boy and Game Boy Color homebrew database from the gbdev community. Entries link a ROM download.

entries.name: gbdev.io
entries.blurb: Front door to the Game Boy development community, with Pan Docs, tool lists and community links.

entries.name: NESdev
entries.blurb: Wiki and forum for NES and Famicom programmers. Most documented NES homebrew technique starts here.

entries.name: SMS Power!
entries.blurb: Master System, Game Gear and SG-1000 site with a homebrew section and the SMS Power Coding Competition.

entries.name: N64brew
entries.blurb: Wiki and community for Nintendo 64 homebrew, and the host of the N64brew Game Jam.

entries.name: AtariAge
entries.blurb: Forums, a software database and a store for Atari homebrew, including new 2600, 5200 and 7800 cartridges.

entries.name: CSDb
entries.blurb: The Commodore 64 Scene Database. It catalogs games, demos and music releases by group.

entries.name: Spectrum Computing
entries.blurb: ZX Spectrum database and forum that includes new releases next to the classics.

entries.name: MSX Resource Center
entries.blurb: News, forums and a software database for MSX, where new homebrew still appears.

entries.name: Neo Geo Dev Wiki
entries.blurb: Technical wiki for programming the Neo Geo, from memory maps to the sprite system.

entries.name: Universal-DB
entries.blurb: Database of Nintendo DS and 3DS homebrew apps and games, maintained by Universal-Team.

entries.name: Open Shop Channel
entries.blurb: Homebrew app store for the Wii, with a web catalog you can browse before touching the console.

entries.name: Homebrew App Store
entries.blurb: Package repository for Switch and Wii U homebrew. It installs from the console and keeps its source and releases on GitHub.

entries.name: VitaDB
entries.blurb: Catalog of PlayStation Vita homebrew games, ports and tools, maintained by Rinnegatamante.

entries.name: ROMhacking.net homebrew
entries.blurb: The original homebrew section of ROMhacking.net, separate from its patches and translations.

entries.name: PSX-Place PS2 homebrew
entries.blurb: Resource index for PS2 homebrew games and ports, with reviews, downloads and a separate section for tools.

entries.name: PSX-Place PS3 homebrew
entries.blurb: Resource index for PS3 homebrew games, with community reviews and download links.

entries.name: Video Game Homebrew Wiki
entries.blurb: Community wiki with a page per homebrew game, covering releases across many platforms.

entries.name: r/Homebrews
entries.blurb: Subreddit for new homebrew releases, development updates and physical cartridge projects across platforms.

entries.name: PICO-8
entries.blurb: Fantasy console with a 128x128 screen and 16 colors. A finished game is one PNG image you can pass around.

entries.name: Lexaloffle BBS
entries.blurb: The forum where PICO-8 carts are posted. Every cart plays in the browser.

entries.name: TIC-80
entries.blurb: Free and open source fantasy computer with a built-in code, sprite and music editor and a public cart library.

entries.name: WASM-4
entries.blurb: Fantasy console where games are WebAssembly modules, so you can write them in Rust, Zig, C or AssemblyScript.

entries.name: Pyxel
entries.blurb: Retro game engine for Python with 16 colors and four sound channels.

entries.name: Uxn
entries.blurb: A tiny virtual machine from Hundred Rabbits. Programs are a few kilobytes and run on anything from a Game Boy to a laptop.

entries.name: Arduboy
entries.blurb: Credit card sized open source handheld with a monochrome OLED. Games are Arduino sketches.

entries.name: Gamebuino META
entries.blurb: Open source handheld for learning to program games, with an online library of community titles.

entries.name: Thumby
entries.blurb: Keychain sized console from TinyCircuits with a 72x40 screen, programmed in MicroPython.

entries.name: Celeste Classic
entries.blurb: Maddy Thorson and Noel Berry built this PICO-8 platformer in four days. It became Celeste.

entries.name: Micro Mages
entries.blurb: Four-player co-op platformer by Morphcat Games, released on a real NES cartridge in 2019.

entries.name: POOM
entries.blurb: A Doom-style first person shooter running inside PICO-8's memory and CPU limits.

entries.name: Super Tilt Bro.
entries.blurb: Platform fighter for the NES in the style of Smash Bros., by sgadrat.

entries.name: Tobu Tobu Girl
entries.blurb: Vertical-scrolling arcade game for the Game Boy by Tangram Games.

entries.name: Xeno Crisis
entries.blurb: Twin-stick shooter by Bitmap Bureau, released on a Sega Genesis cartridge in 2019.

entries.name: Gunlord
entries.blurb: Side-scrolling shooter by NG:DEV.TEAM, released for Neo Geo and Dreamcast in 2012.

entries.name: Bitmap Bureau
entries.blurb: UK studio behind Xeno Crisis and Final Vendetta.

entries.name: NG:DEV.TEAM
entries.blurb: German team that has released Last Hope, Fast Striker and Gunlord on Neo Geo and Dreamcast.

entries.name: Mega Cat Studios
entries.blurb: Pittsburgh studio and publisher of new games for classic consoles.

entries.name: Piko Interactive
entries.blurb: Publisher making new physical games for retro systems alongside licensed re-releases, with cartridges for Atari, Neo Geo and other platforms.

entries.name: CollectorVision
entries.blurb: New ColecoVision games and hardware, sold as cartridges.

entries.name: Super Fighter Team
entries.blurb: Publisher of Beggar Prince and other new Genesis cartridges.

entries.name: Mojon Twins
entries.blurb: Spanish developers who release games for 8-bit machines and publish the engines they use.

entries.name: itch.io Jams
entries.blurb: Calendar of every jam on itch.io. Filter for console-specific ones such as Game Boy and PICO-8 jams.

entries.name: GB Studio
entries.blurb: Visual editor that exports a real Game Boy ROM. You can make a game without writing code.

entries.name: GBDK-2020
entries.blurb: C compiler and libraries for the Game Boy, Master System and Game Gear.

entries.name: Pan Docs
entries.blurb: The Game Boy technical reference. Registers, timing, memory map and cartridge formats.

entries.name: SGDK
entries.blurb: Sega Mega Drive and Genesis development kit in C, with sprite, sound and tile libraries.

entries.name: cc65
entries.blurb: C compiler and assembler for 6502 machines, including the NES, Commodore 64 and Atari 8-bit.

entries.name: devkitPro
entries.blurb: Toolchains and libraries for Game Boy Advance, DS, 3DS, Wii, Wii U and Switch homebrew.

entries.name: libdragon
entries.blurb: Open source SDK for writing Nintendo 64 games.

entries.name: Wonderful Toolchain
entries.blurb: Toolchain for the WonderSwan and other unusual targets.

entries.name: RetroArch
entries.blurb: Front end that runs emulator cores for most systems in this list, on PC, phones and handhelds.

entries.name: Batocera
entries.blurb: Linux distribution that boots straight into a retro game library from a USB stick.

entries.name: Recalbox
entries.blurb: Retro gaming OS for Raspberry Pi and PC with a controller-first menu.

entries.name: MiSTer FPGA
entries.blurb: Open source FPGA project that recreates old consoles and computers in hardware, with cores for new homebrew.

entries.name: Krikzz
entries.blurb: Maker of the EverDrive flash carts, which run homebrew ROMs on real hardware from an SD card.

entries.name: muOS
entries.blurb: Custom operating system for Anbernic handhelds.

entries.name: ROCKNIX
entries.blurb: Linux distribution for retro handhelds based on Rockchip and other chips.

entries.name: Knulli
entries.blurb: Batocera-based firmware for handheld consoles.
